text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock ticked up 0.44% today, capping a strong five-day rally that has lifted it nearly 12% since November 6th. The gains are driven by a tightening refining environment: US refineries are running at 95.2% capacity while heating oil storage sits at unusually low levels (103.33 million barrels) heading into winter—and heating oil prices have spiked 59% year-over-year. For a major refiner, tight product inventories and high heating demand translate directly into better margins and stronger pricing power.

That said, the broader oil picture is complicated. Russian crude production has rebounded sharply after Trump-era sanctions easing, pushing global markets back into oversupply according to the International Energy Agency, which typically weighs on crude prices and refiner feedstock economics. Oil prices have drifted sideways (US crude near $89.62/barrel), which may cap the upside from the tight product story alone.
